drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 79-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.86, creatinine 1.04-1.05, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 285-294, sodium 141, wbc 6.2-6.3; vitals dbp 73-77, heart_rate 85-90, map 93-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 132-139, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.01, hemoglobin 12.9-13, platelets 287, sodium 141, wbc 5.9-6.1; vitals dbp 74-77, heart_rate 86-89, map 94-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 133-136, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 79-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Acute kidney injury. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
